---
title: "Fitting & Inference"
description: "Fit a model to empirical data, tune it, and infer parameters — with the theory that explains when it works."
---

Simulating a model is one thing; making it *match data* is another. This topic covers
fitting model parameters to empirical measurements, tuning a network into a target
regime, and inferring parameter distributions — plus the background on when gradient
optimization is trustworthy.

These workflows run on the **tvboptim** JAX backend (JIT-compiled, autodiff,
GPU-capable). If you arrived wanting to know how TVBO relates to tvboptim as a *tool*,
see [coming from tvboptim](../Interoperability/tvboptim/index.qmd).

## Do

| Goal | Guide |
|---|---|
| Match empirical BOLD functional connectivity | [Reduced Wong-Wang](RWW_tvboptim.qmd) |
| Match a MEG frequency gradient | [Jansen-Rit](JR_tvboptim.qmd) |
| Drive regions to a target firing rate (E/I balance) | [EI tuning](EI_Tuning_tvboptim.qmd) |
| Estimate posteriors over parameters | [Bayesian inference](Bayesian_tvboptim.qmd) |
| Trade off competing objectives | [Multi-objective (Hopf-Pareto)](Hopf_Pareto_tvboptim.qmd) |
| Fit conduction speed / delays | [Delay & speed synchronization](Delay_Speed_Synchronization_tvboptim.qmd) |

## Understand

- [Model fitting](ModelFitting.qmd) — how losses and gradients work in TVBO, and what
  makes a model differentiable.
- [Gradient stability & truncated BPTT](TBPTT_tvboptim.qmd) — why gradients through long
  chaotic trajectories explode, and what truncation buys you.
